thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A managed, automated drone-network service for fire/emergency reconnaissance, including docked dispatch and Skyflow pilots who continuously monitor flights and can intervene. The company positions it against this problem: Fire and emergency-control rooms need rapid overhead incident information before ground crews can safely assess a scene. Verified current scope: City of Munich customer pilot across two drone sites, expanding to three; more than 20 missions reported by February 2026. Stated ambition: networked emergency-response coverage across municipalities. Public evidence supports responsibility for integration and remote operations; supports only partial/shared responsibility for hardware, models/policies, commissioning/qualification and ongoing support/maintenance; does not establish responsibility for robot body, end effectors/tooling, simulation/training and hardware financing/RaaS. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; technical evidence: 4_named_partner_confirmed. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
